title: [spec-gap][R-05-106/109] GPSR attempted before LOADng in all stacks; Rust coord decode skips range validation (spec 9.7)
description: Spec 9.7: GPSR is a last resort - attempted only when (1) no gradient, (2) LOADng RREQ timed out, (3) Yggdrasil fallback unavailable, (4) dest coords known, (5) at least one neighbor has coords. Also: latitude MUST be within +/-90, longitude within +/-180. Classification: divergent. (a) Ordering: all three stacks attempt GPSR BEFORE LOADng and before RPL/BR fallback - rust hybrid.rs:264-289 (gradient then GPSR then LOADng then RPL parent), C router.c:682-689 (GPSR then LOADng at :689), python router.py:543-552 (GPSR when loadng is None). This changes which paths consume airtime. (b) Rust GeoCoords::from_app_data (rust/lichen-node/src/gradient.rs:55-69) scans for byte 0x01 and reads two BE i32 e7 values WITHOUT the plus/minus 90/180 validation that C (router.c:1035-1054 is_valid_coords_e7) and Python (announce/coords.py:78-100) enforce; test/vectors/announce_coords.json is consumed by C and Python but has NO Rust consumer. Suggested placement: (a) decide reorder route_mesh_local (LOADng before GPSR) vs amend spec 9.7 ordering - decision needed; (b) add e7 range validation in gradient.rs from_app_data and add a Rust consumer test for announce_coords.json.
